subject.title: plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride is ignored for interactive (client-scoped) subagent runs

question: Should the shipped `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride` grant authorize plugin subagent provider/model overrides from interactive and other request-scoped contexts, including whether plugin HTTP route scopes are covered?
rationale: Current SDK docs and the reported workflow expect the opt-in to authorize subagent model overrides generally, but shipped release behavior and config wording scoped the grant to background/fallback runs, making this an authorization-boundary and upgrade-semantics choice.

options.title: Approve Widened Grant
options.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

options.title: Narrow Scoped Contexts
options.body: Revise the fix to cover interactive/operator-scoped plugin runs while excluding external plugin HTTP route scopes if maintainers want that boundary preserved.

options.title: Keep Background-Only
options.body: Reject the behavior change and update SDK docs plus runtime errors so operators know this config key cannot authorize interactive plugin subagent overrides.

recommendation.title: Approve Widened Grant
recommendation.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant shipped plugin subagent override policy and tests trace most directly to the merged feature work authored by this owner candidate.
